title: Characterizing Feedback Statements in Machine Learning Jupyter Notebooks
abstract: arXiv:2609.22912v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Machine learning development in Jupyter notebooks is iterative and feedback-driven. Practitioners author statements that reveal information about program execution and use it to decide what to do next. We call these feedback statements and identify two forms: exploratory statements that display values for visual inspection, and validation statements that enforce conditions programmatically through assertions. Many ML failures do not surface as exceptions and thus escape the crash-based analyses that dominate prior work on ML notebooks. This study examines what practitioners check to catch failures that would otherwise pass silently, by characterizing feedback statements that encode the practitioner's mental model of what the code should do and what could go wrong. translated_title: 机器学习Jupyter笔记本中反馈语句的特征刻画
translated_abstract: 在Jupyter笔记本中进行机器学习开发是迭代式且由反馈驱动的。实践者会编写能够揭示程序执行信息的语句，并利用这些信息来决定下一步该做什么。我们将这类语句称为反馈语句，并识别出两种形式：探索性语句（显示数值以供视觉检查）和验证性语句（通过断言以编程方式强制执行条件）。许多机器学习故障并不会以异常的形式显现，因此逃过了以往机器学习笔记本研究中占主导地位的基于崩溃的分析。本研究通过刻画反馈语句来考察实践者会检查什么，以捕获那些原本会静默通过的故障，这些反馈语句编码了实践者关于代码应该做什么以及可能出什么问题的心理模型。我们从GitHub和Kaggle挖掘了297,851个公开的Python Jupyter笔记本，并提取了1,092,780条反馈语句，随后通过比例分层抽样抽取了816条语句进行分析。
tldr: 该研究从近30万个公开Jupyter笔记本中挖掘出百万余条反馈语句，首次系统刻画了机器学习实践者用于捕获静默故障的探索性与验证性两类反馈语句，弥补了以往仅依赖崩溃分析的不足。
en_tdlr: This study mines over one million feedback statements from nearly 300,000 public Jupyter notebooks to systematically characterize exploratory and validation statements that ML practitioners use to catch silent failures escaping crash-based analyses.
